summary: Specifies the Quote of the Day service, which sends a short message without regard to the input. It is an Internet Standard for hosts that choose to implement it.

eli5.summary: A computer that hands you one short saying whenever you ask, like a fortune cookie.

questions: what is the quote of the day protocol
how does qotd work over tcp
subtitle: A tiny service that answers any request with one short quote, on port 17.

tldr.problem: Engineers want a trivial service that returns a short message regardless of input, to debug and measure network connections.
tldr.mechanism: A server on port 17 sends a short quote over TCP and then closes the connection, or sends one UDP datagram containing a quote. Any received data is ignored.
tldr.outcome: The RFC is an Internet Standard for hosts that choose to implement it. The quote has no required syntax, but it should be under 512 characters.

today: RFC 865 is an Internet Standard and has not been obsoleted or updated, so it remains the definition of the Quote of the Day Protocol.

sections.title: A Quote of the Day Service
sections.content:
RFC 865 defines the Quote of the Day Protocol. The RFC calls a quote of the day service a useful debugging and measurement tool that simply sends a short message without regard to the input.

Hosts on the ARPA Internet that choose to implement it are expected to adopt this standard.
sections.eli5: It is a machine that gives out one short saying whenever anyone asks, and does not care what you said.

sections.title: The TCP and UDP Services
sections.content:
Over TCP, a server listens on TCP port 17. When a connection is established it sends a short message and discards any data it receives. The service then closes the connection after sending the quote.

Over UDP, a server listens on UDP port 17. When a datagram arrives, the server sends an answering datagram containing a quote, and the data in the received datagram is ignored. (The RFC's section headings for both services say "Character Generator Service", which looks like a leftover from RFC 864.)
sections.eli5: With TCP you connect, get your quote, and the machine hangs up. With UDP you send a note and get one quote back.

sections.title: Quote Syntax
sections.content: There is no specific syntax for the quote. The RFC recommends limiting it to the ASCII printing characters, space, carriage return and line feed. The quote may be one line or several, but it should be less than 512 characters.
sections.eli5: The quote can be any short saying made of ordinary letters and symbols. Keep it short, like a fortune cookie slip.
